correctness.rationale: The actual age is all finite 1,2,3 metrics additionally omitting 111 and 122; 113 is already nonmetric. Cherlin explicitly identifies this class. Independently, strong amalgamation puts distance 2 across the two sides when a base point is at distance 1 from both and 3 otherwise. A cross 2 with a base 1,2 triangle would violate 122 on one side using the common witness. Two cross 2's and a within-side 1 are also impossible: their witnesses are distinct, at distance 2 via the outside point, and force a 113 triangle on the side with the within-side 1. All remaining mixed triangles are allowed. Homogeneity then identifies types with labelled diagrams. Reconstruct the pair count by the per-coordinate allowed (a,b) with fixed mutual distance: over base 2 each unary word may not mix 1 and 2, giving the stated two-row inclusion–exclusion; over base 3 each row has at most one 1, giving coefficient extraction at degrees (0 or 1,0 or 1). An independent transfer count verifies all six formulas through n=200. For n≥6 the two upper tails lie on opposite sides of 3/5 by the positive quadratic bound, and the lower tails lie on opposite sides of (4/9)(3/4)^n by Q>4P and the rational bound for the distance-2 base. The exact n=2,3,4,5 cross-products match and are strictly positive. Leading terms give the probability vectors and both rare short-channel constants.
residual_risks: Equilateral named bases and injective ordered pairs only; uniform on logical types, not on points. The recurrence experiment alone is not an all-n proof.
